anchors.name: 目标检测器的单源域泛化
anchors.query: We study single-domain generalization for object detection, where a detector is trained on a single labeled source domain and evaluated on unseen target domains without access to target-domain data during training. Methods learn domain-invariant representations or introduce training objectives that improve robustness to distribution shifts while preserving localization and classification accuracy.

anchors.name: 风格迁移与图像转换驱动的检测泛化
anchors.query: We investigate style transfer and image-to-image translation for improving the generalization of object detectors trained on a single source domain. Appearance-diverse training images simulate unseen visual domains and reduce reliance on source-specific textures, illumination, and rendering styles without requiring target-domain samples.

anchors.name: 风格增强与域随机化
anchors.query: We explore style augmentation and domain randomization for single-source domain generalization in object detection. Methods perturb image appearance, feature statistics, textures, or environmental conditions to expand the source-domain distribution and improve detection robustness under unseen domain shifts.

anchors.name: 保持语义、边界框与小目标细节的外观变换
anchors.query: We develop content-preserving appearance transformations for domain-generalized object detection that maintain object identity, spatial geometry, bounding-box alignment, and fine-grained details of small objects. Semantic consistency, structure preservation, and detection-aware constraints prevent style transfer or augmentation from corrupting annotations and localization cues.

anchors.name: 跨域检测的泛化机制与失效分析
anchors.query: We analyze the mechanisms underlying cross-domain robustness in object detectors, including sensitivity to appearance shifts, texture bias, and the transferability of learned representations. Evaluation on real-world cross-domain detection benchmarks combines controlled ablations with failure analysis across object scales and domain-shift conditions to explain when generalization methods succeed or fail.
